q: Malaria is caused by which type of pathogen?
why: Plasmodium, a protozoan, causes malaria and is transmitted by Anopheles mosquito.
Salmonella typhi bacterium causes typhoid, spread via contaminated food/water.

q: HIV mainly attacks which cells, weakening immunity?
why: HIV destroys helper T-lymphocytes, crippling the immune response.

q: Which test is used to confirm typhoid?
why: The Widal test detects antibodies against Salmonella typhi.

q: Immunity present from birth, without prior exposure to a pathogen, is called:
why: Innate immunity is the natural, non-specific defense present from birth.

q: Vaccination works by introducing a weakened or dead pathogen to stimulate:
why: Vaccines trigger the immune system to produce memory cells and antibodies without causing full disease.

q: Uncontrolled and abnormal cell division leading to tumour formation describes:
why: Cancer is characterized by uncontrolled, abnormal cell proliferation.

q: Long-term alcohol abuse is most strongly linked to damage of which organ?
why: Chronic alcohol abuse commonly causes liver cirrhosis and damage.

q: AIDS patients usually die due to:
why: With immunity destroyed, other infections that a healthy body would resist become fatal.

q: Which of the following is NOT a common mode of HIV transmission?
why: Unlike malaria, HIV is not transmitted by mosquito bites.
